The idea · 02

The price keeps moving.
Nobody looks again.

A hotel room is priced like an airline seat — it changes daily. But a booking is treated as final the moment it is paid.

One room, one price, forty-two days

The room was refundable the whole time. Rebooking on day 31 and cancelling the first booking would have returned ₹1,400 — the guest never knew.

~40% of hotel reservations drop in price after they are booked1
67% the largest drops recorded on a single reservation1
0 rechecks a typical guest makes between booking and the free-cancellation deadline
1 ~40% of hotel reservations drop in price after booking, by up to 67% — Pruvo via Travolution Chart is illustrative of one tracked booking, not aggregate data
The idea · 03

Four kinds of traveller,
one shared habit.

They book a refundable room weeks early to lock it in — then never look at the price again.

Families on holiday

Book early for school holidays, often two rooms, and rarely recheck.

Pilgrims

Fixed dates, booked months ahead, prices swing hard near the season.

Weekend getaways

Grab a room the moment a long weekend appears, then stop looking.

Small business travellers

Pay themselves, claim it back, and gain directly from any drop.

All four book refundable rooms early — the exact window in which about 40% of reservations get cheaper.
1 ~40% of hotel reservations drop in price after booking, by up to 67% — Pruvo via Travolution Photographs: Wikimedia Commons — see Sources
The idea · 04

Add it once. We do the looking.

No account linking, no new booking habit. The guest keeps booking wherever they already book.

1

Add the booking

Forward the confirmation email, send a screenshot, paste a link, or message it on WhatsApp. Pay the trip fee by UPI.

About 20 seconds
2

We watch it daily

The same hotel, the same dates, the same room type — rechecked every day until the deadline.

Roughly 20 checks
3

We alert on a drop

WhatsApp, push or email the moment a cheaper price appears, with the deadline shown.

Within the day
4

Rebook and save

Guided steps: book the cheaper room first, check it, then cancel the old one. The saving is recorded.

The guest keeps all of it
We never touch the guest's account or card. Every booking and cancellation stays in the app they already use — we only tell them when, and point them at the cheaper room.
Tracking stops automatically at the free-cancellation deadline, after which a drop is of no use

The idea · 06

Forty-two days, from the guest's side.

One real-shaped booking, end to end. Everything between day 0 and the alert happens without them.

Day 0

Booking added

Forwards the confirmation, confirms what we read, and pays the trip fee by UPI.

Days 1–8

Quiet watching

A daily price check against the same hotel and dates. No messages — silence is the product working.

Day 9

Drop found · alert

₹5,000 seen on Agoda, confirmed by a second check. Alert names the site, the time, and the days left to cancel free.

Day 9

Rebooked

Books the cheaper room first, then cancels the original. Order matters — we show it that way round.

Day 10

Saving recorded

₹1,400 added to their total — all of it theirs. The fee was paid once, on day 0.

Day 40

Tracking ends

Watching stops at the cancellation deadline. Booking data is dropped once there is nothing left to do.

The guest acts twice in forty-two days: once to add the booking, once to rebook. Everything else is ours.
Illustrative timeline using the ₹6,400 → ₹5,000 example carried through the deck

Market · 08

Six people already do a piece of this.

None of them does all of it in India, and the closest one launched three weeks ago.

Onto

Bengaluru

Launched 22 Oct 2026 with $1M pre-seed. Refunds the drop to the original payment method, including bookings made elsewhere. Says 1 in 2 bookings got a refund.1

The direct competitor

Pruvo

Israel

Founded 2016, $1.1M seed. Forward the email to an address, free to the traveller; earns through B2B rebooking for agencies.2

Free · the pricing problem

DreamCheaper

Berlin

Cancels and rebooks automatically, and charges 20% of the saving. Automatic rebooking is where we could grow; a cut of the saving is not our model.3

Automatic rebooking

HotelSlash

United States

A $29.95 a year membership. Tracks and alerts; the traveller rebooks. A yearly fee is a bigger ask in India than one small fee per trip.4

Subscription

Google Hotels

Global

Free price-drop email alerts, but per property and before you book — it does not know what you paid or when you must cancel by.5

Pre-booking only

MakeMyTrip

India

Price Drop Protection exists — but it is flights only, ₹229 domestic and ₹349 international per person, and only on their own bookings.6

No hotel equivalent

Market · 10

The corner nobody holds.

Work with any booking site, and hand back money without touching the booking. Onto is the one company moving into the same corner.

Automatic refund Alert only Only its own bookings Any booking site MakeMyTrip · flights HotelSlash Pruvo Google Hotels DreamCheaper Onto StayWatch

Why not the top-right corner

Automatic refunds need the booking to be ours. That is slide 29's work — company, GST, TBO — not week one.

What we hold instead

OTA-neutral from day one, on WhatsApp without an install, in Telugu, Hindi and English. Onto is well funded but English-first.

The honest risk

Onto can move down into guided rebooking faster than we can move up into refunds. Speed matters more than features.

Placement is our judgement from each company's public description, not a measured study
Market · 11

Six things that could sink this.

Written down plainly, with what we would actually do about each. None of them is solved yet.

01

A free competitor

Pruvo is free and Onto refunds the whole drop. Paying ₹50–150 before any drop is a harder sell.

Mitigation — fee scaled to the booking; automatic refund if we cannot track it.

02

We cannot see every price

Coupons, bank offers and cashback never reach the price feed, so a "drop" may not beat what was actually paid.

Mitigation — compare against the amount paid; alert only on drops of ₹500 and 5% or more.

03

Matching the right room

"Deluxe Double" on one site is "Superior King" on another. The weak point: 60–80% today.

Mitigation — same site, same room, refundable rate, checked twice — or no alert.

04

Only free-cancellation bookings

A non-refundable booking cannot be rebooked, so a drop is worthless — ruling out a real share of the market.

Mitigation — say so at sign-up; push the pre-booking target-price alert.

05

Booking sites may push back

We send cancellations their way. A platform could block affiliate links or change terms.

Mitigation — licensed APIs only, affiliate links for rebooks, never scrape behind a login.

06

Trust

We ask a stranger to forward their name, dates and what they paid. A lot for a new brand.

Mitigation — never ask for passwords or OTPs; one-tap deletion, stated up front.

Mitigations are proposals for discussion, not decisions already taken
Market · 12

Six reasons to pick us.

Each one is a gap in what already exists, not a feature we like the sound of.

App and WhatsApp

WhatsApp removes the install, which is most of the drop-off. Pruvo is email-only; HotelSlash needs you to book through them.

Any booking site

Works with the app the guest already uses. MakeMyTrip's protection covers only MakeMyTrip, and only flights.

Telugu, Hindi, English

The alert that matters arrives in the language the guest thinks in. Every competitor here is English-first.

Target-price alert

Set a price before booking and we tell you when the room reaches it — the one feature that also works on non-refundable plans.

The saving stays with the guest

One fee of ₹50–150 per trip, paid once. No subscription, and never a cut of what the guest saves.

Affiliate rebooking

The rebook goes through our link, so a successful saving also earns 4–5% commission — paid by the site, not the guest.1

Said in one line: the only India-first tracker that works with bookings you already made, reaches you on WhatsApp, and leaves every rupee of the saving with the guest.
1 Agoda ~4–5% by volume — Creator Hero · Booking.com 4% via CJ — MakeInfluence

Product · 16

Safe with no support team.

There is no support staff at launch. So the product has to stay safe even when an alert is wrong.

The rule on every alert

Book the new room first. Check it. Then cancel the old one.

A wrong alert then costs the guest a few minutes — never money, never their room. This protects us more than anything else.

Support target 1–3 issues per 100 trips, almost all closed by the buttons on the alert.
01

Check twice

Re-check the price just before sending. Alert only if the second check agrees.

02

Real drops only

At least ₹500 and at least 5% below what the guest paid.

03

Same room, or silence

Same site, same room name, refundable rate. Not sure? Don't send.

04

Careful words

"Price seen at ₹5,000 on Agoda at 3:10 pm" — never "You will save ₹1,400".

05

Buttons, not tickets

Wrong hotel · Price not there · Stop tracking. Each fixes itself and teaches the matcher.

06

One-tap deletion

The trip and its data go in one tap. We never ask for a card number, OTP or password.

Guidance to finalise before the beta — not fixed policy. Deletion duties under the DPDP Act are on slide 23.

How we build it · 19

Where the prices come from.

The booking sites already publish their prices to Google. We read Google, through a licensed API — we never scrape a booking site.

1

Booking sites publish

MakeMyTrip, Goibibo, Booking.com and Agoda send their rates to Google Hotels themselves.1

2

SerpApi reads Google

A property token returns featured prices and the price per site, by room.2

3

We compare

Same hotel, same dates, against the amount the guest actually paid.

4

We alert

Only when the gap clears a margin and the deadline has not passed.

Why this works in India

MakeMyTrip appears in 52% of sponsored and over 70% of organic Google Hotels listings in India.3 Reading Google reaches the dominant seller without touching its site.

It is also the legal position we want: a licensed API, public data, no login, no fake accounts.

What it cannot see

Coupons, bank offers and wallet cashback are invisible. Some small and OYO-only properties are missing. We get the cheapest room per site, not every room type.

Validation gate — before any code: run 20 real hotels through the free 250 searches and measure how many match. If coverage is poor, the idea stops here.

1 Google: prices come from partners — Google Travel Help 2 property_token → prices per site — SerpApi 3 52% sponsored / 70%+ organic — Skift
How we build it · 20

One source now, three in reserve.

Depending on a single price feed is the biggest technical risk in the product.

MVP · chosen

SerpApi

Google Hotels prices by property token. Free 250 searches a month to validate, then $75 for 5,000.1

Risk — one vendor between us and every price.

Backup

MakCorps · Apify

MakCorps covers 200+ sites; Apify has a Google Hotels actor. Swapped in if SerpApi coverage or health drops.2

Why not first — less predictable, and a second bill.

Earns money

Agoda · Booking.com

Affiliate APIs give prices and pay for the rebook: Agoda about 4–5%, Booking.com 4% through CJ.3

Catch — only their own inventory, so coverage is partial.

Later

TBO

India-strong B2B hotel API. The route to owning the booking and refunding automatically — needs agency registration and KYC.4

Blocked on — company, GST, approval.

Do not plan on Amadeus. The Self-Service API portal shut down on 17 July 2026. Any tutorial recommending it is out of date.5
1 SerpApi pricing 2 MakCorps · Apify 3 Agoda · Booking.com 4 Vervotech 5 PhocusWire
How we build it · 21

How often the alert is right.

Each alert passes three steps. Two are solid. The third — finding the same room and rate — is the weak point.

Likely accuracy, step by step
AI reads the bookingthen the guest confirms it
~98%
Finds the right hotelguest confirms the photo and address
95–99%
Finds the same room and rateroom type, meal plan, free cancellation, guests, taxes
60–80%
0%50%100%

SerpApi returns the cheapest price per site — often a different room or a non-refundable rate. Sent unfiltered, about 1 in 3 alerts would be wrong or unusable.

With the safeguards on slide 16 90–95% of alerts correct — under 5–10% false. Every alert is checked twice and only sent when the room and rate match.

Never 100%

Coupons, bank offers, member prices and cached prices never reach us. That is why every alert says book first, check, then cancel.

Estimates, not measurements — the November validation on slide 29 measures them on 20 real hotels

Legal · 23

What the law lets us do —
and what we will not do.

Three rulebooks shape the product: how we read prices, how we hold data, how we message.

IT Act 2000

Unauthorised extraction is a civil matter under Sec 43 — criminal only when done dishonestly.

Sec 43 — civil liabilityCompensation for unauthorised access
Sec 66 — only if dishonestUp to 3 years or ₹5 lakh
Site terms are a contractContract Act · Copyright Act 1957

DPDP Act 2023

Booking details are personal data. Rules 2025 phase in — main obligations from 13 May 2027.

Explicit consent at sign-upPlain notice of what we read and why
Security safeguardsEncrypted at rest, least-privilege access
Deletion on requestBooking data dropped when tracking ends

WhatsApp policy

Banned for general-purpose AI bots since 15 Jan 2026. Task-specific bots stay allowed.

Task-specific bot onlyNever an open-ended assistant
Approved utility templatesPre-approved · about ₹0.115 per message
The user messages firstWe never open a conversation first
We never log into a user's booking account, never use fake accounts, never bypass a CAPTCHA. Not legal advice — a startup lawyer reviews this before launch.
1 IT Act Sec 43 / 66 — LawRato 2 DPDP Rules 2025 phases — ComplianceHub 3 WhatsApp bot policy — respond.io
Legal · 24

Who got this right,
and who got sued.

Five cases that draw the line we intend to stay well inside.

Did it right

CamelCamelCamel

Tracks Amazon prices through Amazon's own licensed API — never scraped.1

Did it right

BuyHatke

An extension reads the page the user is already on, funded by affiliate links.2

Lost

hiQ v LinkedIn

Won on public data, lost on the terms — fake accounts, $500k judgment.3

Allowed

Meta v Bright Data

Logged-out public data did not breach Meta's terms. The line is logging in.4

Still running

Ryanair v Booking.com

Scraping behind a login drew a US jury verdict, overturned in 2025 and under appeal. Unsettled law — so we avoid logins entirely.5

Our rules

PracticeAllowedNot allowed
Read prices through SerpApi
Use affiliate APIs for prices
Send rebooks via affiliate links
Log into a user's account
Fake accounts or CAPTCHA bypass
Scrape behind a login

Money · 25

We charge for the watching, not the win.

One small fee per trip, paid when the booking goes in. Whatever the guest saves is theirs.

Primary · launch price

₹50–150 per trip

Paid by UPI when the booking is added, before tracking starts. Covers that trip until its free-cancellation deadline.

The range is set; the exact fee is agreed after discussion.

Secondary

Affiliate on rebooks

The rebook goes through our link. Agoda pays about 4–5% by volume, Booking.com 4% on completed stays via CJ.1

Paid by the booking site, never by the guest.

What we never do

Take a cut of the saving

If the room drops ₹1,400, the guest keeps ₹1,400. No share, no subscription, no second charge.

Nothing to prove after the fact, so no disputes over what was really saved.

Setting the fee — three options to discuss

Flat ₹99 a trip · By booking value ₹50 under ₹5,000, ₹99 to ₹15,000, ₹150 above · By nights ₹50 a night, capped at ₹150.

Open question — what if nothing drops?

Most trips will not (slide 27). Keep the fee, or carry it to the next trip. Either way, refund automatically if we cannot track the hotel.

1 Agoda ~4–5% by volume — Creator Hero · Booking.com 4% via CJ — MakeInfluence Fees shown before GST

Per 100 paid trips₹50 fee₹100 fee₹150 fee
Fees collected₹5,000₹10,000₹15,000
Cost to watch, today₹2,800₹2,900₹3,100
Left for us₹2,200₹7,100₹11,900
Plus affiliate on rebooks₹1,000–1,500
Saved by the guests₹10,000–21,000

At ₹150 the guests, as a group, get back roughly what they paid. At ₹50 they get back 2–4 times as much.

Every fee in the range is profitable for us. The question is what the guest feels — keep the fee well below a typical saving, which argues for ₹50–99 on smaller bookings.
Funnel and costs are our estimates, not measurements. Assumes a ₹1,000–1,400 average saving, a ₹5,000 average rebooking, and half of rebooks through an Agoda or Booking.com link at 4%.
Launch · 28

Getting the first hundred.

One number does the selling: the rupees a real person got back. Everything below is a way of showing it.

First 100 users

Hand-picked, by hand

Family, college, hostel and local travel WhatsApp groups. We add their bookings for them, by hand if we must.

Timing

Launch into a peak

December–January, Sankranti, summer, pilgrimage seasons, long weekends, weddings — people book early for all of them.

Content

Reels, in three languages

"I saved ₹2,700 after I had already booked" in Telugu, Hindi and English. The alert, then the refund. Thirty seconds.

Distribution

Micro-creators

Regional travel accounts, 10–100k followers, paid per post. Cheaper than ads and more trusted for a money claim.

Compounding

SEO pages

"Price dropped after booking — can I rebook?" per city and per site. Slow, but it pays after the spend stops.

Loop

Referral on the saving

The moment someone is told they saved is the moment they share. Put the referral there, nowhere else.

The goal of the first hundred is not revenue. It is thirty screenshots of real savings — without those, none of the channels above work.
Peak-season framing follows the pilgrimage and domestic-travel growth cited on slide 07

The plan, with gates.

Each stage has something that must be true before the next one starts. The first gate can stop the whole idea.

November

Validate

20 real hotels through SerpApi's free 250 searches.

Gate — if coverage and accuracy are poor, stop here.

Week 1–2

Design and setup

Screens, database, WhatsApp number approved, templates submitted.

Gate — templates approved before any build.

Week 3–6

Build the MVP

The ten features on slide 13, and nothing else.

Gate — one booking tracked end to end.

Week 7–8

Free beta · 30–100 users

People we can reach directly. One segment — pilgrims or one city. MakeMyTrip, Booking.com and Agoda only.

Gate — 90% of alerts correct.

Jan 2027

Paid launch · ₹50–150

Fee agreed after discussion, switched on for new trips. Thirty real savings to show.

Gate — false alerts under 5%, or no fee.

After

Store launch, then TBO

Play and App Store. Then company, GST and TBO approval for own bookings, B2B for agents, new categories.

Validation comes before design, and the beta is free on purpose: no payments means no payment complaints while the matcher is still learning.

Launch · 30

What this becomes if it works.

Each step removes work from the guest. The end state is that they never have to act at all.

01

Auto cancel and rebook

We do both sides and the difference comes back automatically. Needs the booking to be ours — which is what TBO unlocks.

02

Book with us

Price protection built into the booking itself. The guest stops thinking about rebooking because we already handle it.

03

Price prediction

Enough tracked bookings become a dataset: "this hotel usually drops 12 days out — wait." Advice before the booking, not after.

04

Beyond hotels

Buses are refundable and repriced constantly. Then homestays and packages. The same loop, different inventory.

05

Travel-agent dashboard

An agent re-prices a hundred client bookings at once. Fewer customers, far larger each, no consumer marketing spend.

06

Trip assistant in WhatsApp

Task-specific only — rebooking, deadlines, prices. A general assistant would break WhatsApp policy, so it stays narrow.1

The through-line: today we tell the guest, tomorrow we do it for them, eventually they book with us and it never comes up.
1 Task-specific bots remain allowed; general-purpose AI bots banned from 15 Jan 2026 — respond.io
Launch · 31

Eight numbers we watch.

Three of them can kill the business on their own. Those three have targets; the rest are for learning.

VolumePaid tripsThe top of everything. Nothing else matters if this is flat.
Does the idea hold% with a dropPruvo's ~40% is the claim.1 Our own number decides whether this is a product.
Size of the winAverage ₹ savedHas to sit well above the fee, or guests stop paying for the next trip.
Does the alert workAlert → rebookIf people are told and do nothing, the alert is wrong, not the guest.
Trust · target < 5%False-alert rateThe one that destroys the product fastest. Measured every week of the beta.
Viability · target ≤ ₹30Cost per tripRises quietly as hotels get rechecked more often. The fee minus this is our margin.
HabitRepeat usersSecond booking added within 90 days. Travel is infrequent, so this is slow.
Load · target 1–3Issues per 100Per 100 trips. Almost all should close through the buttons on the alert.
1 ~40% of reservations drop in price after booking — Pruvo via Travolution
Verdict · 32

The honest verdict.

Three of the four questions have a confident answer. The fourth is the reason the beta comes first.

Can we build it? Yes

High confidence.

Every part is an existing, licensed service. Nothing here is research.

Is it safe for guests? Yes

If we keep two rules.

Book first, then cancel — and a second price check before every alert.

Will alerts be accurate? Mostly

Good enough. Perfect, never.

90–95% correct with the safeguards. Coupons and bank offers stay invisible.

Will the business work? Uncertain

The real question.

Onto is funded and refunds the difference. Google's price alerts are free. We ask ₹50–150 up front.

Our edge has to be WhatsApp, Indian languages and any booking app — and a fee small enough that a guest who sees no drop still feels it was worth it.
Accuracy figures are estimates until the November validation on slide 29. Competitor facts as sourced on slide 08.
